svg.text: B. How a fight picks its slice
A touch-down point and a great circle through it; the circle is kept when it meets Orb's minimum. Then the circle is read as the arena.
Random on the planet (or named by a story level).
The great circle through T and each city (grey), plus a few of random bearing.
3 Test, in a seeded order, the first that passes wins (pink)
- at least 2 cities and 3 towns within reach of the line
- at least 3 biomes of 8% each, at least half of it land
- none passes (about 8% of touch-downs with 12 cities): move T, or relax to one city + five towns
4 Read the circle as the arena
column i sits at p(i) = cos(i x 32 / R) u + sin(i x 32 / R) v
u = T, v = (n x T): only sin, cos and sqrt, our own and exact. No inverse trig.
height(p), biome(p) come from the planet's function; places come from the list.
The arena: 153,600 units, 4,800 columns, wrapping (T is the middle; the ends meet).
Settlement boxes are the width of the line's chord through the settlement; the label under each says how far off its centre the line passes.
A line through a city's middle shows its downtown; a line near the edge shows only its outskirts (figure E).
2 cities, 4 towns, 4 biomes, 70% land, 28% of the length is settled. Found on candidate 1.
Same seed, same touch-down, same circle: nothing about the choice depends on the machine.
